labels.definition: Seasonal, food and drug allergies, anaphylaxis and allergy treatment, including allergy drugs (which take this label alone).
labels.name: Allergies & anaphylaxis

labels.definition: Endocrine function outside reproductive hormones. Sex hormones go to `womens` or `mens` when the sex is specified, otherwise to `endocrine.hormone_balance`; stress experience and regulation practices to `stress`.
labels.name: Hormones, Thyroid & Adrenal

labels.definition: Hormones in general, "hormone balance" talk spanning several hormones, and sex hormones discussed with no sex specified.
labels.name: Hormone balance (general)

labels.definition: Thyroid function and disease and its treatment.
labels.name: Thyroid

labels.definition: Cortisol as a hormone (its levels, rhythm, testing and effects such as belly fat) and adrenal function and disorders. "Cortisol" used only as a word for feeling stressed goes to `stress.stress_burnout`.
labels.name: Cortisol & adrenal function

labels.definition: Growth hormone, IGF-1, DHEA, pregnenolone, oxytocin, melatonin as a hormone, leptin, ghrelin and similar, when the hormone's levels, physiology or use are discussed. A hormone used for physique or performance also takes its `peds` subtopic; insulin goes to `metabolic.insulin_glucose`; oxytocin as the "love hormone" in talk about bonding goes to `cognition.neurochemistry_talk`.
labels.name: Other hormones

labels.definition: Kidney, urinary and lung health. Respiratory infections go to `infectious`; allergies to `immune.allergies`.
labels.name: Kidneys, Bladder & Lungs

labels.definition: Kidney disease and function, kidney stones, dialysis, and bladder and urinary problems such as incontinence and overactive bladder. A urinary tract infection as an infection goes to `infectious.other_infections`, adding this subtopic only when bladder or urinary health beyond the infection is discussed; prostate-related urination goes to `mens.prostate`.
labels.name: Kidneys & urinary tract

labels.definition: Lung disease and lung function.
labels.name: Lungs & breathing

labels.definition: Cancer as a disease: causes, rates, screening, diagnosis and conventional treatment. Alternative remedies go to `cancer_alt`; tobacco, sun or chemical exposures also take their own subtopics.
labels.name: Cancer

labels.definition: What causes cancer, what raises or lowers the risk of getting it, and how common it is: carcinogens and exposures, foods, drugs or habits said to cause, feed or prevent cancer in people without it, risk factors, trends, early-onset cancer, cancer as a "metabolic" disease. Treating an existing cancer with a diet, food or remedy goes to `cancer_alt`.
labels.name: Cancer causes, risk, prevention & rates

labels.definition: Detecting cancer: screening tests and diagnostic workups. Elective full-body scans go to `self_tracking.body_scans`, adding this subtopic when they are discussed as cancer screening.
labels.name: Cancer screening & diagnosis

labels.definition: Standard oncology: chemotherapy, radiation, surgery, immunotherapy, targeted drugs, cancer vaccines and cell therapies, supportive care for treatment side effects, cancer centers and survivorship. Chemotherapy for a non-cancer disease takes that disease's subtopic.
labels.name: Conventional cancer treatment

labels.definition: Breast cancer specifically.
labels.name: Breast cancer

labels.definition: Melanoma and other skin cancers.
labels.name: Skin cancer

labels.definition: Prostate cancer specifically, including PSA testing for it.
labels.name: Prostate cancer

labels.definition: Any other named cancer type.
labels.name: Other named cancers

labels.definition: Colon, rectal and bowel cancer specifically, including the rise in early-onset colorectal cancer. Screening for it also takes `cancer.screening_diagnosis`.
labels.name: Colorectal cancer

labels.definition: Non-standard cancer treatments, complementary add-ons to standard care, and refusals of standard care. The suppressed-cure storyline is a narrative (`narrative:cancer_cures_suppressed`).
labels.name: Alternative Cancer Treatments

labels.definition: Off-label drugs promoted for cancer, when cancer is named. The same drugs sold or discussed with no cancer named go to `medications.repurposed_offlabel`, and inside a parasite protocol to `detox.parasite_cleanses`.
labels.name: Repurposed drugs for cancer

labels.definition: Diets and fasting presented as treating or starving cancer. Used alongside standard treatment, they go to `cancer_alt.integrative_adjuncts`.
labels.name: Dietary & metabolic cancer approaches

labels.definition: Herbal, mushroom, vitamin, IV and folk remedies for cancer. Mind, faith or energy healing of cancer takes `stress.mind_body` or `alt_medicine.energy_spiritual_healing` plus the bare `cancer_alt` parent.
labels.name: Natural & IV cancer remedies

labels.definition: Clinics and named protocols outside standard oncology. Hyperthermia counts here only as a cancer therapy; heat illness goes to `acute_care.poisoning_environmental_injury`.
labels.name: Alternative cancer clinics & protocols

labels.definition: Choosing to forgo or delay chemotherapy, surgery or radiation, and the outcomes. Treatment the oncologist judged unnecessary is `cancer.conventional_treatment`.
labels.name: Refusing or delaying standard treatment

labels.definition: Complementary therapies used alongside chemotherapy, radiation or surgery (hyperbaric oxygen, supplements, fasting or ketosis around treatment, melatonin), as opposed to replacements for them. A conventional drug added to chemotherapy, and standard supportive care, go to `cancer.conventional_treatment`.
labels.name: Integrative add-ons to standard cancer care

labels.definition: Conditions of the brain and nervous system. Dementia goes to `dementia_ageing`; mental-health conditions to `mental`; cognitive performance to `cognition`.
labels.name: Neurological Conditions

labels.definition: Stroke, aneurysm and other cerebrovascular events.
labels.name: Stroke & cerebrovascular disease

labels.definition: Seizure disorders.
labels.name: Seizures & epilepsy

labels.definition: Headaches and migraine as symptoms or conditions, and their treatment.
labels.name: Headache & migraine

labels.definition: Traumatic brain injury and its long-term effects, from any cause. A sport concussion takes this subtopic only, not also `musculoskeletal.sports_injuries`; a brain injury from a crash, fall or assault takes this rather than `acute_care.trauma_fractures` for that injury.
labels.name: Concussion & brain injury

labels.definition: Progressive neurological disease other than dementia. MS also takes `immune.autoimmune`.
labels.name: Neurodegenerative & movement disorders

labels.definition: Peripheral nerve and spinal cord problems, paralysis as a medical condition, and neural implants used to treat it. Sleep paralysis goes to `sleep`.
labels.name: Nerves, spinal cord & paralysis

labels.definition: Named neurological conditions not listed above. Tinnitus goes to `sensory.hearing`.
labels.name: Other neurological conditions

labels.definition: Age-related cognitive change and decline, and the care of older people. Longevity protocols go to `longevity`.
labels.name: Dementia, Ageing & Elder Care

labels.definition: Dementia and Alzheimer's: what it is, causes, diagnosis, drugs and prevention claims, including "cognitive decline" used to mean dementia risk. Normal age-related cognitive change, and an older leader's sharpness debated with no dementia claimed, go to `dementia_ageing.cognitive_ageing`.
labels.name: Alzheimer's & dementia

labels.definition: Caring for older people, long-term care, and age-related frailty and falls. Caregiving for children is not this subtopic.
labels.name: Elder care & frailty

labels.definition: Age-related cognitive change and mental capacity in older people short of dementia, including debate over an older leader's mental sharpness when no dementia is claimed.
labels.name: Normal cognitive ageing

labels.definition: Musculoskeletal pain, injury and rehabilitation. Acute trauma goes to `acute_care`.
labels.name: Pain, Bones, Joints & Muscles

labels.definition: Spinal pain and posture.
labels.name: Back pain, neck pain & posture

labels.definition: Joint pain and joint disease. Rheumatoid, psoriatic and other inflammatory arthritis go to `immune.autoimmune`, adding this subtopic when joint symptoms or damage are discussed.
labels.name: Joints & arthritis

labels.definition: Bone density and bone strength.
labels.name: Bone health & osteoporosis

labels.definition: Named injuries from sport, training or repetitive use, whoever the person, and their rehabilitation and surgery. Concussions go to `neuro.concussion_tbi`; injuries from a fall, crash or assault to `acute_care.trauma_fractures`.
labels.name: Sports & overuse injuries

labels.definition: Persistent pain and how it is managed, other than opioids, including mind-body approaches to pain. Fibromyalgia goes to `chronic_complex.fibromyalgia`.
labels.name: Chronic pain & pain management

labels.definition: Physical therapy, rehabilitation, exercise prescribed to recover from an injury or pain, and conventional manual therapy. General stretching goes to `fitness.mobility_flexibility`; chiropractic to `alt_medicine.chiropractic`; pelvic-floor therapy to `womens.pelvic_floor`.
labels.name: Physical therapy & rehabilitation

labels.definition: Muscle mass as a health outcome: losing, keeping or building it for health (with age, disuse, fasting or drugs), and muscle as an organ of health. How to train goes to `fitness.strength_training`.
labels.name: Muscle mass & sarcopenia

labels.definition: Acute injury and emergency care, and death and dying. In crime, war, news or history, a killing, wound, cause of death or autopsy told only as part of the story is not health content (codebook section 3); these subtopics apply when the medical side (care, survival, disability, a medical explanation, or an autopsy finding of disease, overdose, poisoning, starvation or neglect) is itself described.
labels.name: Injuries, Emergencies & End of Life

labels.definition: Cuts, burns and bites, and what bystanders do immediately about them or about collapse, choking or bleeding, before professional care. Resuscitation in hospital goes to `acute_care.emergency_critical_care`; cuts and stitches in sport to `musculoskeletal.sports_injuries`.
labels.name: Wounds, burns & first aid

labels.definition: Physical injuries from a fall, crash, assault, combat or other non-sport cause, and an unspecified injury to a real person, when the injury, its treatment or recovery is described. A wound told only as part of a crime or war story is not this subtopic; a brain injury goes to `neuro.concussion_tbi`.
labels.name: Injuries & trauma

labels.definition: Interpersonal violence and abuse discussed as a pattern, risk, prevention or health and safety issue (sexual assault, domestic violence, child abuse and neglect, gun violence as a public-health matter, elder abuse), a survivor's harm and recovery, and emotional or psychological abuse in relationships as harm. A single crime, or an allegation against a named person, told as a story, news or legal process is not this subtopic; therapy-speak as a social phenomenon goes to `mental.pop_psychology`.
labels.name: Violence & abuse

labels.definition: Emergency departments, ICUs, sepsis, shock, resuscitation, organ failure.
labels.name: Emergency & critical care

labels.definition: Poisoning, overdoses of non-drugs-of-abuse, heat illness, hypothermia, drowning, choking, altitude, G-forces, motion and seasickness. Food poisoning goes to `infectious.foodborne`.
labels.name: Poisoning, environmental & motion injury

labels.definition: How people die and end-of-life care: dying as a process, causes of death as medical fact, autopsy findings of disease, overdose or neglect, hospice, palliative care, advance directives, death doulas, euthanasia and assisted dying. A death named only as a fact about a person ("died of cancer", "died of a heart attack") takes the cause's subtopic alone.
labels.name: Death, dying & end-of-life care

labels.definition: Experiences reported during clinical death, cardiac arrest or a near-fatal event (leaving the body, a tunnel or light, a life review) and claims about what they show about consciousness or death. "A near-death experience" meaning only a close call takes the event's own subtopic.
labels.name: Near-death experiences

labels.definition: Operations, clinical procedures, clinical lab tests and blood or cell therapies that are not cosmetic, weight-loss or cancer-specific.
labels.name: Surgery & Medical Procedures

labels.definition: Operations, recovery and the experience of being hospitalized, when the operation or stay is itself discussed. A procedure named only as the treatment of a condition with its own subtopic ("had ACL surgery", "gender surgery", "plastic surgery", "LASIK") takes that subtopic instead.
labels.name: Surgery & hospital stays

labels.definition: Anesthesia and sedation.
labels.name: Anesthesia

labels.definition: Organ and tissue transplant and blood or organ donation.
labels.name: Transplants & donation

labels.definition: Medical imaging and diagnostic procedures outside cancer screening, and radiation dose from them. Prenatal ultrasound goes to `pregnancy.pregnancy_health` (and `fertility.abortion` in pregnancy-center appeals); elective full-body scans to `self_tracking.body_scans`; blood and lab tests to `procedures.lab_testing`. Imaging cited only as a research method ("MRI studies show") is not this subtopic.
labels.name: Imaging & diagnostic procedures

labels.definition: Clinician-ordered blood and lab tests, panels, reference ranges and their interpretation. Tests a consumer orders or buys directly go to `self_tracking.consumer_lab_tests`.
labels.name: Clinical lab testing & blood work

concepts: stem cells in Mexico or Panama
labels.definition: Stem-cell, platelet, exosome and similar therapies, and supplements claimed to mobilize stem cells, used for healing, orthopedic or systemic disease rather than appearance.
labels.name: Regenerative medicine (non-cosmetic)

labels.definition: Therapeutic plasma exchange, transfusion, cord-blood banking and cell infusions (NK cells), conventional or experimental. Used as a longevity protocol, they also take `longevity.protocols_clinics`.
labels.name: Blood, plasma & cell therapies

labels.definition: The senses and their loss, correction and aids.
labels.name: Eyes, Ears & Senses

labels.definition: Eyes and sight, eye disease and eye-care products. Screens or blue light blamed for eye harm also take `radiation_light.artificial_light`.
labels.name: Vision & eye health

labels.definition: Hearing, ears, and balance or vestibular problems. Motion and seasickness go to `acute_care.poisoning_environmental_injury`.
labels.name: Hearing, ears & balance

labels.definition: Smell, taste and ear-nose-throat structures. Loss of smell or taste from COVID also takes `covid.illness_severity`; sinus infections go to `infectious.respiratory_common`.
labels.name: Smell, taste, nose & throat

labels.definition: Teeth, gums and the mouth, including fluoride.
labels.name: Oral & Dental Health

labels.definition: Fluoride added to public water: its effects and the policy fights over it.
labels.name: Water fluoridation

labels.definition: Fluoride toothpaste, varnish, drops and tablets and other fluoride treatments, and their alternatives.
labels.name: Fluoride & fluoride-free dental products

labels.definition: Dental work and dental materials, orthodontics and aligners, cosmetic dentistry, jaw problems and teeth grinding, and holistic or biological dentistry as a practice. Tongue-tie release takes this label plus `pregnancy.infant_feeding` when about latch and feeding, or `sleep.apnea_breathing` when about the airway.
labels.name: Dental procedures, materials & dentistry

concepts: oral health is linked to heart disease
labels.definition: Cavities, gum disease, the oral microbiome, oral health as a driver of disease elsewhere in the body, and hygiene practices.
labels.name: Oral hygiene & gum health

labels.definition: Heredity and genetic explanation, testing and therapy.
labels.name: Genetics & Heredity

labels.definition: What is inherited and how; genetic risk variants (APOE4, BRCA as a risk gene); genes versus lifestyle; epigenetics as gene expression changed by lifestyle or exposures, and epigenetic inheritance. Epigenetic clocks go to `longevity.biological_age`.
labels.name: Inheritance, genetic risk & gene expression

labels.definition: Genetic and genomic testing, consumer or clinical, embryo screening, and DNA-based health or nutrition reports. An MTHFR variant discussed as a gene or test takes this label; advice to take methylated vitamins because of it takes `supplements.b_vitamins_methylation` (both when both).
labels.name: Genetic testing

labels.definition: Conditions with a genetic or congenital cause.
labels.name: Genetic & congenital conditions

labels.definition: Altering genes to treat or enhance. Calling mRNA vaccines "gene therapy" takes `vaccines.covid_vaccines` (and `narrative:mrna_alters_dna`), not this label, unless gene therapy as a technology is itself discussed.
labels.name: Gene editing & gene therapy

labels.definition: Chronic, hard-to-diagnose or contested multi-symptom illnesses, persistent infections offered as their cause, and the patient communities around them. Long COVID goes to `covid.long_covid`; acute infections go to `infectious`.
labels.name: Contested & Complex Chronic Illness

labels.definition: Lyme disease as a persistent or relapsing illness, and its co-infections. Persistence may be implied by relapse or long-term or repeated treatment; Lyme told only as an acute infection goes to `infectious.vector_borne`, other persistent infections to `chronic_complex.persistent_infections`.
labels.name: Chronic Lyme & co-infections

labels.definition: Myalgic encephalomyelitis / chronic fatigue syndrome, and chronic fatigue presented as a condition or diagnosis. "Chronic fatigue" named only as a symptom or in an ad testimonial goes to `wellness.energy_fatigue`; post-COVID cases also take `covid.long_covid`.
labels.name: ME/CFS & chronic fatigue

labels.definition: Autonomic dysfunction.
labels.name: POTS & dysautonomia

labels.definition: Mast cell activation syndrome and histamine reactions attributed to mast cells, hypermobility disorders and Ehlers-Danlos syndrome. Dietary histamine intolerance stays in `gut.candida_histamine`; "hypermobile" meaning joint range in training is not this label.
labels.name: MCAS, histamine reactions & Ehlers-Danlos

concepts: I had a severe mold exposure
labels.definition: Mold or biotoxin illness as a diagnosis or as the explanation for symptoms. When the same passage also covers finding or remediating mold in a building, add `environment.indoor_air_mold`; mold allergy goes to `immune.allergies`.
labels.name: Mold illness & CIRS

labels.definition: Fibromyalgia.
labels.name: Fibromyalgia

labels.definition: The experience of living with chronic, undiagnosed or multiple illnesses and of seeking care for them: medical gaslighting, dismissal, diagnostic odysseys, patient communities. "Chronic illness" as a general category or trend goes to `wellness.chronic_disease_trends`.
labels.name: Living with chronic illness

labels.definition: Latent, persistent or reactivated infections invoked to explain chronic symptoms or disease: Epstein-Barr and other herpesvirus reactivation, mycoplasma, and "stealth" or "hidden" infections. The condition explained also takes its own subtopic (EBV and Hashimoto's: `endocrine.thyroid` and `immune.autoimmune`); chronic Lyme goes to `chronic_complex.chronic_lyme`, long COVID to `covid.long_covid`, an acute infection (mono, a shingles outbreak) to its `infectious` subtopic. The claim that such infections underlie most chronic disease is `narrative:stealth_infections_root`.
labels.name: Persistent, reactivated & "hidden" infections

labels.definition: Named multi-symptom illnesses attributed to an exposure, weapon or implant whose cause or recognition is disputed, other than mold and Lyme: Havana syndrome, Gulf War illness, breast implant illness, multiple chemical sensitivity, electromagnetic hypersensitivity, Morgellons. Also code the exposure's or injury's subtopic when its harm is discussed (`neuro.concussion_tbi`, `skin_beauty.cosmetic_procedures`, `radiation_light.wireless_emf`).
labels.name: Exposure & implant syndromes

labels.definition: Psychiatric conditions, their diagnosis, treatment and care, and psychological wellbeing. General "mental health" with nothing more specific takes this parent. Autism and ADHD go to `neurodevelopment`; stress physiology and regulation practices to `stress`.
labels.name: Mental Health & Psychiatry

labels.definition: Depression as a condition or a sustained depressive state, named as such: diagnosis, episodes, symptoms, treatment, rates. Low mood short of that goes to `mental.wellbeing_grief_loneliness`; a momentary reaction ("I'm so depressed we lost") is not health content.
labels.name: Depression

labels.definition: Anxiety disorders, panic attacks, and anxiety as an ongoing condition or symptom. Ordinary worry or nervousness about an event is not health content.
labels.name: Anxiety & panic

labels.definition: Psychological trauma and its effects, including PTSD, childhood adversity, and repressed or recovered memories of trauma. Trauma said to cause physical illness also takes `stress.mind_body`; brain injury goes to `neuro.concussion_tbi` and physical injury to `acute_care.trauma_fractures`.
labels.name: Trauma & PTSD

labels.definition: Serious mental illness.
labels.name: Bipolar, psychosis & schizophrenia

labels.definition: OCD and related disorders (body dysmorphia included), intrusive thoughts in the clinical sense, personality disorders and traits as clinical categories (psychopathy included), and factitious disorder (Munchausen syndrome; Munchausen by proxy also takes `acute_care.violence_abuse` as medical child abuse). Muscle dysmorphia goes to `manosphere.male_body_image`. Insults and loose description ("a narcissist", "a psychopath", "a little OCD", "intrusive thought" for a hot take, "Munchausen" as a jibe) are not health content.
labels.name: OCD, intrusive thoughts, personality & factitious disorders

labels.definition: Suicide, suicidal ideation and self-harm.
labels.name: Suicide & self-harm

labels.definition: Eating disorders and disordered eating.
labels.name: Eating disorders

labels.definition: Psychiatric drugs: effects, side effects, withdrawal, prescribing. ADHD stimulants go to `neurodevelopment.adhd`.
labels.name: Psychiatric medications

labels.definition: Talk therapy of all kinds and access to it.
labels.name: Psychotherapy & counseling

labels.definition: Psychological wellbeing as a subject: happiness, loneliness, grief and bereavement, purpose, resilience, burnout as emotional state, and mood (low or good mood, mood swings, irritability) short of a diagnosed disorder. A real person's grief or loneliness narrated as part of a story is not this label unless the state itself or its effects are discussed.
labels.name: Wellbeing, mood, grief & loneliness

labels.definition: Popular psychological vocabulary (therapy-speak), self-diagnosis as a social phenomenon, self-help about spotting and handling "narcissists", attachment styles, and claims that mental-health diagnoses in general are over-applied or normal feelings pathologized. Abuse in a relationship discussed as harm goes to `acute_care.violence_abuse`; narcissistic personality disorder as a diagnosis to `mental.ocd_personality`; overdiagnosis of one disorder also takes that disorder's subtopic.
labels.name: Pop psychology & self-diagnosis

labels.definition: Compulsive behaviors treated as an addiction or disorder: loss of control, harm, treatment, recovery. Casual "I'm addicted to my phone" about heavy use goes to `cognition.digital_media_brain`.
labels.name: Behavioral addictions

labels.definition: General theories of what causes mental illness (trauma, perception, inflammation, metabolism and diet, chemical imbalance, social determinants) not tied to one disorder.
labels.name: Causes & models of mental illness

labels.definition: How psychiatric care is delivered, accessed and enforced: psychiatric hospitals and holds, involuntary commitment, asylums and deinstitutionalization, access to psychiatrists (psychiatric telehealth included), non-drug somatic treatments (ECT, TMS, stellate ganglion block, lobotomy as history), and psychiatric evaluation in the courts (insanity defense, competency). Drugs go to `mental.psychiatric_drugs`, talk therapy to `mental.therapy`, ketamine and psychedelics to `psychoactives`, general hospital care to `health_system.hospitals_access`; the person's condition also takes its own subtopic. "Insane asylum" as a jibe is not health content.
labels.name: Psychiatric care, hospitalization & forensic psychiatry

labels.definition: Autism, ADHD and other neurodevelopmental conditions.
labels.name: Autism, ADHD & Neurodevelopment

labels.definition: Why autism occurs and how common it is: genetics, environmental causes, diagnostic changes, the "autism epidemic", the HHS autism report.
labels.name: Autism causes & prevalence

labels.definition: Therapies and claimed treatments or cures for autism. Leucovorin for autism takes this and `supplements.b_vitamins_methylation`.
labels.name: Autism treatment & cure claims

labels.definition: ADHD diagnosis, prevalence and treatment, including prescribed stimulant medication. Stimulants taken without ADHD to study or work go to `cognition.nootropics` and party use to `drugs_addiction.stimulants_illicit`; a simile ("like I took an Adderall") is not health content.
labels.name: ADHD

labels.definition: Neurodivergence as identity, culture and accommodation, and everyday life with autism for autistic people and their families: adult and late diagnosis, masking, support needs, nonverbal communication, school and work. Causes and rates go to `neurodevelopment.autism_causes_prevalence`; therapies to `neurodevelopment.autism_treatment`.
labels.name: Neurodiversity & living with autism

labels.definition: Speech, motor and learning delays, learning disabilities, intellectual disability, and tic disorders beginning in childhood or adolescence (Tourette's, functional tics). Genetic syndromes (Down syndrome) go to `genetics.genetic_conditions`; tics beginning in adulthood to `neuro.other_neurological`.
labels.name: Developmental delays, learning disabilities & tic disorders

labels.definition: Stress as an experience and the practices sold or taught to regulate it. Cortisol as a hormone goes to `endocrine.cortisol_adrenal`.
labels.name: Stress & Nervous-System Regulation

labels.definition: Stress, chronic stress and burnout and their effects on health, including "cortisol" used colloquially to mean stress ("don't spike your cortisol"). Cortisol measured or discussed as a hormone goes to `endocrine.cortisol_adrenal`.
labels.name: Stress & burnout

labels.definition: The vocabulary and practices of nervous-system regulation, including vagus-nerve stimulation devices worn for calm or sleep (which also take `biohacking.devices_gadgets`).
labels.name: Nervous-system regulation

labels.definition: Breathing practices for stress, performance or healing. Breathing during sleep goes to `sleep.apnea_breathing`.
labels.name: Breathwork

labels.definition: Meditation, mindfulness and contemplative practice.
labels.name: Meditation & mindfulness

labels.definition: Time outdoors and physical contact with the earth (earthing) as health practices, and products sold for it. "Grounding" meaning calming or stabilizing is not this label.
labels.name: Nature exposure & grounding

labels.definition: Emotions, beliefs, trauma, social connection and psychological state said to affect physical illness, immunity or recovery (psychoneuroimmunology, psychosomatic illness). "Mind-body connection" as a product slogan or as exercise technique is not this label.
labels.name: Mind-body connection

labels.definition: Sleep quality, duration, timing and disorders, and products and practices aimed at them.
labels.name: Sleep

labels.definition: How much and how well people sleep, naps, and sleep as the outcome of a factor.
labels.name: Sleep duration & quality

labels.definition: Trouble falling or staying asleep and its treatment.
labels.name: Insomnia & sleep medication

labels.definition: Breathing during sleep, daytime mouth breathing and airway development.
labels.name: Breathing, airway & sleep apnea

labels.definition: Body clocks, and light at night or light timing affecting sleep or melatonin. Daytime effects of screens and LED light on the eyes, mood or health go to `radiation_light.artificial_light`.
labels.name: Circadian rhythm & light timing

labels.definition: Practices and products for sleep: bedtime routines (children's included) and the bedroom (mattresses, temperature, darkness, noise, devices in bed). Newborn sleep safety goes to `pediatrics.infant_care`.
labels.name: Sleep hygiene & sleep environment

labels.definition: Sleep disorders other than insomnia and sleep-disordered breathing, and dreaming as a sleep or brain phenomenon: narcolepsy and hypersomnia, parasomnias (sleep paralysis, sleepwalking, night terrors, sleep talking, REM sleep behaviour disorder), and lucid dreaming, nightmares and what dreams are for, whatever explanation is offered. Trouble sleeping goes to `sleep.insomnia`, apnea to `sleep.apnea_breathing`, restless legs to `neuro.other_neurological`. Recounting what happened in a dream, and "sleepwalking through" something as an idiom, are not health content.
labels.name: Dreams, parasomnias & other sleep disorders

labels.definition: Focus, memory and brain performance in healthy people, and the substances and routines aimed at them. General "brain health" or "brain function" takes this parent.
labels.name: Cognitive Performance & Brain Optimization

labels.definition: Concentration and attention as a capacity of the brain that is trained, impaired or improved (by sleep, diet, practices, substances or devices). Productivity methods, work habits and "attention span" as a cultural complaint with no health claim are not this label.
labels.name: Focus & attention

labels.definition: Substances and branded blends taken to enhance cognition, including prescription stimulants or modafinil used without a diagnosis to study or work. Methylene blue for other purposes goes to `medications.repurposed_offlabel`.
labels.name: Nootropics & smart drugs

labels.definition: Memory, learning and intelligence in healthy people, including IQ as an outcome of an exposure (which also takes the exposure's subtopic). Age-related change goes to `dementia_ageing.cognitive_ageing`; intellectual disability to `neurodevelopment.developmental_delays`; "low IQ" as an insult is not health content.
labels.name: Memory, learning & intelligence

labels.definition: Brain fog as a symptom and its causes. When the fog is discussed in its own right alongside its cause (menopause, long COVID, a diet), also code the cause's subtopic.
labels.name: Brain fog

concepts: serotonin is made in the gut
labels.definition: Popular talk about dopamine, serotonin and other neurotransmitters as levers of behavior or mood, when the brain chemistry is the point. "Dopamine hit" as a bare metaphor for a reward feeling is not health content.
labels.name: Dopamine & neurotransmitter talk

labels.definition: Effects of phones, screens and social media on attention, mood and development, and policies aimed at them (phone-free schools, age limits for children). Compulsive use treated as an addiction or disorder goes to `mental.behavioral_addictions`; "screen time" meaning TV airtime and "brain rot" as an insult are not this label.
labels.name: Screens, social media & the brain

labels.definition: Female reproductive endocrinology and gynecology across the life course. Pregnancy goes to `pregnancy`; fertility, contraception and abortion to `fertility`.
labels.name: Women's Hormonal & Gynecological Health

labels.definition: The cycle and its problems, including lost or absent periods from under-eating, over-training or stopping the pill. Age at first period and early puberty go to `pediatrics.puberty_adolescence`.
labels.name: Menstrual cycle & periods

labels.definition: Estrogen, progesterone and testosterone in women: levels, ratios and testing in any context except menopause. Prescribed hormones go to `womens.hormone_therapy`; progesterone for conception also takes `fertility.infertility_treatment`.
labels.name: Female sex hormones

labels.definition: The menopausal transition and its symptoms, including genitourinary symptoms.
labels.name: Perimenopause & menopause

labels.definition: Prescribed hormones for menopause and testosterone for women, including bioidentical hormones and vaginal estrogen. "HRT" said of men means testosterone replacement (`mens.testosterone`); said of transgender people, `gender.adult_transition` or `gender.youth_gender_medicine`.

labels.name: Wireless & electromagnetic fields

labels.definition: Products and practices sold to block or reduce EMF. A "low-EMF" or "zero-EMF" selling point in an ad for another product (sauna, heating mat, red-light panel) does not take it unless EMF harm is stated.
labels.name: EMF protection products & practices

labels.definition: Sun exposure as a health factor: benefits, harms, tanning, sun avoidance. Sunscreen goes to `skin_beauty.sunscreen`; morning or daytime light viewed to set the body clock goes to `sleep.circadian_light` unless skin, vitamin D or UV effects are also discussed.
labels.name: Sunlight & UV exposure

labels.definition: Screens and LED or blue light affecting the eyes, mood or health in the daytime. Light at night or light timing affecting sleep goes to `sleep.circadian_light`; blue-light glasses take whichever effect is discussed.
labels.name: Artificial light

labels.definition: Radiation from nuclear sources, radon and medical imaging dose.
labels.name: Ionizing & nuclear radiation

labels.definition: Skin, hair and cosmetic concerns and the products and procedures aimed at them. Chemical toxicity of products goes to `environment.household_personal_care`.
labels.name: Skin, Hair & Beauty

labels.definition: Acne and its treatment.
labels.name: Acne

labels.definition: Other skin diseases. Psoriasis also takes `immune.autoimmune`.
labels.name: Skin conditions

labels.definition: Skincare routines and products, and the skin microbiome.
labels.name: Skincare products & routines

labels.definition: Sunscreen: use, ingredients, safety.
labels.name: Sunscreen

labels.definition: Hair loss, thinning, regrowth and greying in any sex, and hair-care products or practices offered for hair health.
labels.name: Hair loss & hair care

labels.definition: Wrinkles, collagen and the look of ageing skin.
labels.name: Skin ageing & appearance

labels.definition: Cosmetic surgery and injectables, including genital cosmetic surgery, loose-skin or body-contouring procedures after weight loss or pregnancy, and breast implant illness and explant surgery. Therapeutic Botox goes to `medications.other_drugs`.
labels.name: Cosmetic surgery & injectables

labels.definition: Platelet, stem-cell, exosome and related treatments for appearance (skin, hair, face), injected or topical. The same therapies for healing or disease go to `procedures.regenerative_medicine`.
labels.name: Regenerative aesthetics

labels.definition: Subjects that exist only in infancy and childhood. Use the population axis, not this parent, for content about children on a subject that has its own subtopic (childhood vaccines take `vaccines`; children's diets take `food` or `diets`).
labels.name: Infant & Child Health (pediatric-specific)

labels.definition: Caring for newborns and infants, including newborn procedures (vitamin K shot, newborn circumcision), NICU care and newborn sleep safety (SIDS, sleep position, co-sleeping). Infant mortality rates go to `pregnancy.maternal_mortality_access`; children's sleep routines to `sleep.sleep_hygiene_environment`.
labels.name: Newborn & infant care

labels.definition: Normal child development, including emotional development, resilience and parenting approaches.
labels.name: Child development & parenting

labels.definition: The experience of children's medical care: pediatric visits, children's dosing and pediatrician relationships. A pediatrician's vaccine advice or a family's vaccine dispute with a pediatrician goes to `vaccines.uptake_hesitancy`, plus this label only when the care relationship itself is discussed; a childhood illness takes its own subtopic plus a population label.
labels.name: Pediatric care

labels.definition: Feeding babies and young children solid food.
labels.name: Baby food & child feeding

labels.definition: Puberty, its timing (age at first period included) and adolescent physical development.
labels.name: Puberty & adolescent development

labels.name: Lifestyle as a whole

concepts: "60% of kids have a chronic condition"
labels.definition: Rising chronic disease in general, across conditions.
labels.name: Chronic disease trends (general)

labels.definition: Building health habits, motivation and coaching for health behaviour. Habits about money or work do not take it; a weight-loss programme's behaviour change goes to `weight.weight_loss_methods`.
labels.name: Habits & behavior change

labels.definition: Population life expectancy and mortality trends. Years of life gained or lost from a specific risk or intervention ("cuts ten years off your life") go to that risk's or intervention's subtopic.
labels.name: Life expectancy & mortality statistics

labels.definition: Tiredness, low energy and afternoon crashes described as a symptom or complaint, outside ME/CFS or a diagnosed condition. Generic energy promises in ad copy ("clean energy", "no crash", "all-day energy") name the product's purpose and do not take it.
labels.name: Energy & everyday fatigue

labels.definition: Health, medicine or wellness content, substantive or passing, that no parent topic fits. Name the subject in the summary. Never use it beside a listed topic on the same span; it exists to make gaps in the taxonomy visible.
labels.name: Other health topic

concepts: the bundle of vaccines triggers autism
the Amish don't vaccinate and don't have autism
labels.definition: **Vaccines cause autism or developmental regression.** Any vaccine or the schedule (often MMR, or the number of shots) is blamed for autism, the rise in autism, or loss of speech and developmental delays after shots; low autism rates in unvaccinated groups such as the Amish are offered as proof.
labels.name: Vaccines cause autism

concepts: aluminum levels off the Richter scale
SV40 in the polio vaccine caused cancer
labels.definition: **A vaccine ingredient or contaminant causes harm.** Aluminum, mercury (thimerosal), formaldehyde, PEG, polysorbate or a contaminant such as SV40 in the old polio vaccine is said to cause neurological damage, allergy, cancer or chronic disease. Objecting to fetal cell lines on moral or religious grounds, with no harm claimed, is not this narrative; DNA contamination of mRNA vaccines is `narrative:mrna_alters_dna`.
labels.name: Vaccine ingredients are toxic

labels.definition: **The number or timing of childhood vaccines causes harm.** The schedule is said to overload the immune system, so spacing shots out is safer; a spacing preference with no harm claimed is not this narrative.
labels.name: Too many vaccines too soon

concepts: newborns aren't sharing needles or having sex
it's for prostitutes and drug users
your perfect baby doesn't need the Hep B vaccine
why give a newborn a sex-disease vaccine
labels.definition: **Newborns of hepatitis-B-negative mothers do not need, or are harmed by, the birth dose.** Reporting that the CDC or ACIP changed the newborn recommendation, without the claim itself, is `topic:vaccines.hep_b` only.
labels.name: Hep B birth dose unnecessary or harmful

labels.definition: **Vaccines cause sudden infant death or other infant deaths.**
labels.name: Vaccines cause SIDS or infant death

concepts: chronic disease rose with the schedule
labels.definition: **Vaccines cause the rise in chronic disease.** Allergies, autoimmunity or the "sickest generation" are blamed on vaccines, and unvaccinated children are said to be healthier.
labels.name: Vaccines drive chronic illness

labels.definition: **Vaccines did not end infectious disease.** Infectious diseases are said to have declined because of sanitation or nutrition instead, or polio is said to have been pesticide (DDT) poisoning.
labels.name: Vaccines did not end infectious disease

concepts: nobody admits there are vaccine injuries
a surveillance system built to fail
nurses let go for filing VAERS reports
labels.definition: **Vaccine injury is far more common than acknowledged because it is hidden, underreported or dismissed.** VAERS is said to capture a tiny fraction, injured people to be gaslit or ignored, or reporting to be discouraged. VAERS counts cited for one specific harm take that harm's narrative and `evidence:official_data_documents` instead, unless underreporting or hidden mass harm is also claimed.
labels.name: Vaccine injury is hidden or underreported

concepts: can't be sued, so the schedule exploded to 70 shots
why do they need liability protection if they're safe
liability shield means no incentive for safety
can't sue Pfizer so why test
labels.definition: **Because makers cannot be sued, vaccines are unsafe or untested, or the schedule expanded for profit.** The liability shield (1986 Act, PREP Act) is the premise; saying the shield exists without one of these conclusions is not this narrative.
labels.name: Vaccine makers have no liability

labels.definition: **Vaccines were never properly tested.** They are said to lack true placebo controls or adequate study. "Safe and effective was a lie" alone is `narrative:covid_vaccine_ineffective`.
labels.name: Vaccines not properly tested

concepts: already had COVID, why do I need the shot
they refused to recognize natural immunity
labels.definition: **Immunity from infection is as good as or better than vaccination, so people who have recovered do not need the vaccine.** Mandates are often said to have wrongly ignored it.
labels.name: Natural immunity is as good as or better than vaccination

labels.definition: **The HPV vaccine causes serious harm,** such as infertility, POTS, autoimmunity or death.
labels.name: HPV vaccine is harmful

concepts: flu shot gave me the flu
labels.definition: **Flu vaccines are useless or harmful,** including causing the flu.
labels.name: Flu shots don't work or cause harm

concepts: athletes dropping dead on the field
more people died in the vaccine arm
labels.definition: **COVID vaccines kill people.** Sudden deaths of young or healthy people and athletes are attributed to them. A sudden death or an athlete's collapse with no vaccine named or plainly implied is not this narrative; add `narrative:excess_deaths_cover_up` only when concealment or ignoring of excess-death data is claimed.
labels.name: COVID vaccines kill / died suddenly

concepts: myocarditis risk higher than from COVID for young men
labels.definition: **COVID vaccine myocarditis is common, serious or concealed.** It is said to be frequent, often fatal or lasting, or downplayed or hidden by officials. Noting the established rare risk in young men without any of these claims is `topic:vaccines.safety_injury`, not this narrative.
labels.name: COVID vaccine myocarditis is widespread

labels.definition: **COVID vaccines cause or accelerate cancers ("turbo cancer").**
labels.name: Turbo cancer

labels.definition: **mRNA vaccines alter DNA or are gene therapy rather than vaccines.** They are said to integrate into the genome or be contaminated with DNA.
labels.name: mRNA vaccines alter DNA or are gene therapy

labels.definition: **Vaccinated people shed vaccine material or spike protein that harms others.**
labels.name: Vaccine shedding

labels.definition: **COVID vaccines harm fertility or pregnancy,** causing infertility, miscarriage or menstrual damage.
labels.name: COVID vaccines harm fertility or pregnancy

concepts: spike protein in the body for years
spike protein detox with nattokinase and bromelain
labels.definition: **Vaccine-made spike protein is toxic or persists in the body, driving ongoing illness,** so it must be cleared or detoxed. Spike protein passed from vaccinated people to others is `narrative:vaccine_shedding`.
labels.name: Vaccine spike protein is toxic and persists

concepts: repeat boosters weaken the immune system
labels.definition: **COVID vaccines don't work.** They are said not to prevent infection, transmission, hospitalization or death, or to make infection worse; "safe and effective was a lie" belongs here.
labels.name: COVID vaccines don't work

concepts: not fatal in a well-nourished nation
labels.definition: **Measles, or another vaccine-preventable childhood infection, is harmless, beneficial or manageable without vaccination.** It is called a mild illness whose deaths are overstated, or vitamin A, cod liver oil, budesonide or good nutrition are said to suffice.
labels.name: Measles and other childhood infections are harmless

concepts: magnets stick to the injection site
labels.definition: **Vaccines contain microchips, 5G components, graphene, magnets or tracking technology.**
labels.name: Vaccines contain microchips or 5G technology

concepts: how many more billions to Pfizer and Moderna
labels.definition: **Vaccines and boosters are pushed mainly for profit by their makers or funders.** Recurring boosters, variant shots and vaccination programmes (often Gates-funded) are cast as revenue schemes. A revenue figure alone ("the most profitable medical product in history") is a premise, not this narrative; the general claim that medicine keeps people sick is `narrative:pharma_creates_customers`.
labels.name: Vaccines are pushed for profit

labels.definition: **SARS-CoV-2 came from a laboratory accident or research in Wuhan.** Contested, not necessarily false.
labels.name: Lab-leak origin

labels.definition: **The virus was made as a weapon or released on purpose, or the pandemic was planned.** A virus engineered in gain-of-function research that leaked by accident is `narrative:covid_lab_leak` only, even when loosely called a "bioweapon"; code both when deliberate weapon-making or deliberate release is asserted.
labels.name: Bioweapon / planned pandemic

labels.definition: **Ivermectin prevents or treats COVID-19.** It is often said to have been suppressed; the suppression on its own is `narrative:early_treatment_suppressed`.
labels.name: Ivermectin treats COVID

labels.definition: **Hydroxychloroquine prevents or treats COVID-19.** It is often said to have been suppressed; the suppression on its own is `narrative:early_treatment_suppressed`.
labels.name: Hydroxychloroquine treats COVID

labels.definition: **Effective early COVID treatments were deliberately suppressed,** to enable vaccine authorization or for profit, including punishing doctors who used them. Silencing of people or information is `narrative:pandemic_censorship`.
labels.name: Early treatment was suppressed

labels.definition: **Hospital protocols killed COVID patients.** Remdesivir, ventilators or hospital incentives are blamed, sometimes with hospitals said to be paid for it.
labels.name: Hospital protocols killed patients

labels.definition: **Masks do not reduce transmission, or they harm wearers** (oxygen, CO2, child development).
labels.name: Masks don't work or cause harm

labels.definition: **Lockdowns and closures caused more harm than they prevented.** Listing their costs without weighing them against what they prevented is not this narrative.
labels.name: Lockdowns did more harm than good

labels.definition: **COVID deaths or cases were overcounted.** Deaths "with" rather than "from" COVID and false-positive PCR tests are the usual elaborations.
labels.name: COVID deaths and cases were inflated

concepts: kids have a 99.99% survival rate so they don't need the vaccine
young healthy people don't need a booster
labels.definition: **COVID was mild or no worse than flu for most people, or for a group such as children, so the response was disproportionate.** The response can be lockdowns, mandates, or vaccinating children and young adults.
labels.name: COVID's danger was exaggerated

labels.definition: **Long COVID is not a real post-infection illness.** It is called psychosomatic, fabricated or actually vaccine injury.
labels.name: Long COVID is not real

concepts: vitamin D levels and COVID deaths
labels.definition: **Vitamin D, zinc, quercetin or similar supplements prevent or treat COVID-19.**
labels.name: Vitamin D or zinc prevents COVID

labels.definition: **Accurate COVID information or dissenting scientists were censored.** Officials, platforms or media are said to have silenced or smeared them, often in coordination. Suppression of a treatment is `narrative:early_treatment_suppressed`.
labels.name: Pandemic dissent was censored

labels.definition: **Effective cancer cures exist but are suppressed** by pharma, doctors or government for profit.
labels.name: Cancer cures are suppressed

labels.definition: **Antiparasitic drugs (ivermectin, fenbendazole, mebendazole) cure or treat cancer.** Antiparasitics take this narrative, not `narrative:natural_remedy_cures_cancer`; a combined protocol takes each narrative whose remedy is named.
labels.name: Antiparasitics cure cancer

labels.definition: **Cancer feeds on sugar, so cutting sugar or a ketogenic diet treats it.** The broader claim that cancer is a metabolic rather than genetic disease is `narrative:cancer_metabolic_disease`; code both when both are made. "Starving cancer" of its blood supply with foods (anti-angiogenesis) is not this narrative.
labels.name: Sugar feeds cancer / keto starves it

concepts: Warburg said the cause of cancer is
labels.definition: **Cancer is fundamentally a metabolic, not a genetic, disease.** Damaged mitochondria are said to drive it, so metabolic or dietary approaches are the real treatment. Discussing the Warburg effect or cancer metabolism as one feature or drug target, without denying the genetic model, is `topic:cancer.causes_rates`.
labels.name: Cancer is a metabolic disease

labels.definition: **Chemotherapy does more harm than good.** It is said to rarely work, kill more than it cures, or spread the cancer.
labels.name: Chemotherapy does more harm than good

concepts: B17 and apricot seeds kill cancer cells
labels.definition: **A specific herb, food or alternative protocol cures or treats existing cancer.** "Fights", "reverses", "heals", "kills cancer cells" and "shrinks tumors" count when said of existing cancer; a food said only to have "anti-cancer properties", to be "cancer-fighting" or to lower cancer risk is not this narrative. Vitamin megadoses are `narrative:vitamin_megadose_cures` and antiparasitic drugs `narrative:antiparasitics_cure_cancer` instead.
labels.name: A natural remedy cures cancer

labels.definition: **Cancer screening causes or spreads cancer, or does more harm than good.**
labels.name: Cancer screening causes harm

labels.definition: **Seed and vegetable oils drive chronic disease,** inflammation or obesity.
labels.name: Seed oils are toxic

concepts: cholesterol is not the bad guy
insulin, not LDL, causes heart disease
labels.definition: **Saturated fat, dietary cholesterol or blood (LDL) cholesterol do not cause heart disease.** The diet-heart or lipid hypothesis is called wrong or fraudulent, high LDL on a low-carb diet is called harmless, cholesterol is called a harmless repair molecule, or high cholesterol is said to mean longer life. Statin harm or uselessness is `narrative:statins_harmful`.
labels.name: Saturated fat and cholesterol do not cause heart disease

concepts: sugar is more addictive than cocaine
labels.definition: **Sugar is uniquely toxic.** Sugar or fructose is said to be addictive like drugs and to drive most chronic disease.
labels.name: Sugar is poison

labels.definition: **Synthetic food dyes cause harm,** such as hyperactivity, ADHD or behavior problems in children, or cancer, and are said to be banned elsewhere for that reason. Reporting a ban or phase-out without the harm claim is `topic:food.additives_dyes` only.
labels.name: Synthetic food dyes are harmful

labels.definition: **Raw milk is healthier or safer than pasteurized milk.** It is said to cure allergies or asthma, or pasteurization is said to destroy its value.
labels.name: Raw milk is superior and safe

labels.definition: **Genetically modified foods damage health.**
labels.name: GMOs are harmful

labels.definition: **Glyphosate in food is poisoning the population,** driving gut damage, cancer, gluten intolerance or chronic disease.
labels.name: Glyphosate is poisoning the population

labels.definition: **Artificial sweeteners cause cancer or other harm,** such as metabolic damage or microbiome harm.
labels.name: Artificial sweeteners cause cancer or harm

concepts: gluten causes leaky gut in everyone
labels.definition: **Gluten or modern wheat harms everyone,** not only people with celiac disease. A claim that grains in general are harmful is `narrative:plants_are_toxic`.
labels.name: Gluten harms everyone

concepts: we're poisoning our kids through food
the people poisoning our food sell us the cure
labels.definition: **Food companies or the government deliberately make food that sickens or poisons people,** sometimes to create patients for pharma. Saying processed food is engineered to be craveable or to make people overeat, with no intent to sicken alleged, is `topic:food.ultra_processed` (with `frame:big_food` if the industry is blamed).
labels.name: The food supply is engineered to make people sick

concepts: I eat pasta in Italy and feel fine
labels.definition: **American food is more harmful than food abroad because of ingredients, additives or pesticides that other countries ban or restrict.** The same product with a different recipe abroad, or feeling fine after eating bread or pasta in Europe, are the usual proofs.
labels.name: US food is more harmful than food abroad

labels.definition: **An all-meat diet cures or reverses disease** such as autoimmune disease, depression or diabetes. "Treats", "heals" and "improves [a disease]" count.
labels.name: Carnivore cures disease

concepts: we don't need to eat gobs of kale
labels.definition: **Plants, grains or plant compounds are harmful or unnecessary for people in general.** Vegetables, oxalates, lectins, fiber or grains are said to damage health or the gut; gluten alone is `narrative:gluten_harms_everyone`. Avoiding a compound because of an individual sensitivity (a low-oxalate diet for oxalate issues) is not this narrative.
labels.name: Plants, grains and vegetables are toxic

labels.definition: **Fasting or a ketogenic diet cures or reverses disease** such as diabetes, autoimmunity, dementia or chronic disease generally. "Treats", "heals" and "improves [a disease]" count; the specific mechanism that sugar feeds cancer is `narrative:sugar_feeds_cancer`.
labels.name: Fasting or keto cures disease

labels.definition: **Alkaline food or water changes blood pH and prevents disease,** or disease thrives in an acidic body.
labels.name: Alkaline diet or water changes body pH

labels.definition: **Structured, hydrogen-rich, raw or "living" water has special health properties.**
labels.name: Structured, hydrogen or raw water

labels.definition: **Soy or phytoestrogens lower testosterone or feminize men.** "Soy boy" used as an insult, with no health claim, is not this narrative.
labels.name: Soy feminizes men

concepts: fries used to be cooked in tallow, real fat, really good for you
labels.definition: **Animal fats are healthier than plant oils.** Beef tallow, lard or butter are offered as better than seed or vegetable oils, as food or skincare; add `narrative:seed_oils_toxic` only when seed oils are also said to cause harm. A product attribute alone ("fried in beef tallow, no seed oils") takes `frame:naturalness_appeal` or `frame:toxin_purity`, not this narrative.
labels.name: Animal fats are healthier than plant oils

concepts: red meat is not the enemy
meat causes cancer is a myth
labels.definition: **Red meat is healthy, and warnings that it causes heart disease, cancer or early death are wrong.**
labels.name: Red meat is healthy

concepts: don't stand in front of the microwave
labels.definition: **Microwave ovens are dangerous: they emit harmful radiation, cause cancer or destroy the nutrients in food.** Chemicals leaching from plastic heated in the microwave are `narrative:household_toxins_poisoning` when harm is claimed, not this narrative.
labels.name: Microwave ovens are dangerous

concepts: soil has no minerals anymore so you have to supplement
you can't get it from food
labels.definition: **Soil depletion means people need supplements.** Modern soil is said to be so depleted that food no longer supplies enough nutrients; depleted soil without "so you need supplements" said or plainly implied is not this narrative.
labels.name: Depleted soil means everyone needs supplements

concepts: a glass of red wine a day
labels.definition: **Moderate drinking, especially red wine, protects the heart or extends life.** The French paradox and the J-curve are the usual support.
labels.name: Moderate drinking is protective

concepts: salt is bad for you is a myth
the demonization of salt over sugar
salt doesn't raise your blood pressure
labels.definition: **Dietary salt is not harmful for most people, and advice to cut it is wrong or harmful.** Salt is said not to raise blood pressure, or low-salt diets are said to be dangerous; sugar is often named as the real culprit. Advice to add electrolytes for exercise or fasting, without disputing salt guidance, is not this narrative.
labels.name: Salt fears are overblown

concepts: the food pyramid ignited the obesity epidemic
the low-fat era made us fat
the food pyramid was a lobbying instrument
labels.definition: **Official dietary guidance (the food pyramid, low-fat advice) caused the obesity and chronic-disease epidemic,** often because grain, sugar or food-industry lobbying shaped it. That dietary fat is harmless is `narrative:saturated_fat_cholesterol_myth`; that the guidelines are industry-controlled, with no harm claim, is `narrative:fda_captured`; deliberate engineering of food is `narrative:food_engineered_to_harm`.
labels.name: Official diet advice caused the obesity epidemic

labels.definition: **Statins do more harm than good or are useless.** They are said to deplete CoQ10, cause diabetes or dementia, or exist for profit.
labels.name: Statins are harmful or useless

labels.definition: **Antidepressants do not work or are no better than placebo.** Saying they do not work for everyone, or are overprescribed, is not this narrative. Claims about the serotonin theory are `narrative:chemical_imbalance_myth`.
labels.name: Antidepressants don't work

concepts: the chemical imbalance theory is not based in real science
the biggest pharma scam is that depression is a chemical imbalance
labels.definition: **The serotonin or "chemical imbalance" theory of depression is false or was a lie.** Describing someone's depression as "a chemical imbalance" without addressing the theory's validity is not this narrative in any stance. Whether the drugs work is `narrative:antidepressants_ineffective`; that depression is not a real illness at all is `narrative:mental_illness_not_real`.
labels.name: The chemical-imbalance theory is a myth

concepts: most mass shooters are on psychiatric drugs
labels.definition: **Psychiatric drugs, especially SSRIs, cause violence, mass shootings or suicide.** Pointing out that a shooter took psychiatric drugs counts when it is offered as the explanation.
labels.name: SSRIs cause violence or shootings

concepts: over-diagnosing anxiety and ADHD in kids
labels.definition: **Therapy culture, over-diagnosis and over-protection harm the resilience of children and young people.**
labels.name: Therapy culture harms children

labels.definition: **Acetaminophen in pregnancy or infancy causes autism or ADHD.** Glutathione depletion is the usual mechanism offered.
labels.name: Acetaminophen in pregnancy causes autism

labels.definition: **Leucovorin (folinic acid) treats or reverses autism.**
labels.name: Leucovorin treats autism

concepts: reducing the fever makes kids sicker longer
labels.definition: **Fever reducers suppress immunity and prolong illness, so fevers should be left untreated.** "Fever is good" counts when it is offered as a reason not to treat the fever.
labels.name: Fever reducers are harmful

concepts: the pill changes who women are attracted to
labels.definition: **Hormonal birth control causes serious harm.** Typical harms named are infertility, depression, suicide, cancer, weight gain, personality or partner-choice change, lowered testosterone, libido loss and sexual pain. A labelled side effect (such as clot risk) stated as known prescribing information, with no wider harm claim, is a topic.
labels.name: Hormonal birth control causes serious harm

labels.definition: **Medication abortion is dangerous,** or causes breast cancer, infertility or depression.
labels.name: The abortion pill is dangerous

labels.definition: **Menopausal hormone therapy causes serious harm and should be avoided,** such as breast cancer or heart disease. A passage arguing the WHI scare was wrong takes `narrative:hrt_fears_overblown` only; add this narrative (rebutted) only when the harm proposition is stated and argued against separately.
labels.name: Menopausal hormone therapy is dangerous

labels.definition: **The WHI-era scare about menopausal hormone therapy was wrong or exaggerated,** and HRT is safe or broadly protective.
labels.name: HRT fears were overblown

labels.definition: **GLP-1 drugs cause serious harm or trap users for life.** Muscle wasting, stomach paralysis, blindness, suicide or cancer are the usual harms. Saying neutrally that people stay on them long term, advising protein or lifting to limit muscle loss, and boxed-warning boilerplate in GLP-1 ads are not this narrative.
labels.name: GLP-1 drugs are dangerous

labels.definition: **ADHD stimulants are harmful or overprescribed.** They are called speed, or said to be given to normal children or adults for convenience. Comparing Adderall to cocaine or meth in a recreational story or joke is not this narrative unless the point is that prescribing it is harmful; that ADHD is not a real condition is `narrative:mental_illness_not_real`.
labels.name: ADHD drugs are harmful or overprescribed

concepts: they want us sick so they can sell drugs
labels.definition: **Medicine or the drug industry keeps people sick, or treats symptoms instead of curing, so that patients stay lifelong customers.** Calling the system "sick care" or reactive takes this only when a profit or keep-them-sick motive is stated or plainly implied; "they want us sick" with a control motive is `narrative:depopulation_agenda`, with the food industry as actor `narrative:food_engineered_to_harm`, and vaccine profit is `narrative:vaccines_for_profit`. Lowered cholesterol thresholds also take `narrative:statins_harmful` only when statin harm or uselessness is stated.
labels.name: Medicine keeps people sick for profit

concepts: medications are the fourth leading cause of death
labels.definition: **Medical care or prescription drugs are a leading cause of death** (e.g. the third or fourth).
labels.name: Medicine is a leading cause of death

labels.definition: **Water fluoridation lowers IQ, harms brain development or is a neurotoxin.** Calcification of the pineal gland claimed as harm, with no control purpose, belongs here.
labels.name: Fluoride lowers IQ / harms the brain

labels.definition: **Fluoride is added to pacify, dumb down or control people.** The pineal gland is often the mechanism, but pineal harm without a stated purpose is `narrative:fluoride_lowers_iq`.
labels.name: Fluoride is used for control

concepts: your teeth are making you sick
labels.definition: **Root canals, amalgams, jawbone cavitations or metal implants cause chronic or systemic disease.** "Cavitation" also names joint popping and shockwave effects, which are not this narrative.
labels.name: Dental work causes systemic disease

labels.definition: **Sunscreen does more harm than good.** It is said to cause cancer, be toxic or block needed vitamin D; sunscreen must be named, and avoiding the sun in general is `narrative:sun_exposure_cures`.
labels.name: Sunscreen is harmful

concepts: sun avoidance kills more than smoking
labels.definition: **Sun exposure prevents or cures many diseases, and avoiding or blocking sunlight causes disease.** Skin cancer is often included, and sunglasses or covering up count as blocking; sunscreen named as harmful is `narrative:sunscreen_harmful`.
labels.name: Sun exposure is a cure-all

labels.definition: **Aluminum antiperspirants cause breast cancer.**
labels.name: Antiperspirant causes breast cancer

concepts: ADHD is not a real disease
a concept invented by the medical industry
labels.definition: **Depression, anxiety, ADHD or other common psychiatric diagnoses are not real illnesses,** but inventions of the medical industry, moral or spiritual failings, or ordinary life. The serotonin theory alone is `narrative:chemical_imbalance_myth`; whether the drugs work is `narrative:antidepressants_ineffective`.
labels.name: Common mental illnesses are not real

concepts: your labs are normal but you're not
labels.definition: **Standard lab tests and reference ranges routinely miss thyroid, hormone or metabolic dysfunction, so people told their labs are normal are often sick.** Full panels and narrow "optimal ranges" are said to be needed. One patient's missed diagnosis without the general claim is `topic:health_system.medical_errors`.
labels.name: "Normal" lab results hide real disease

labels.definition: **Germs, or a specific pathogen, do not cause the disease attributed to them.** Viruses are said not to exist or not to be contagious and the "terrain" is all that matters, or a named pathogen is denied its role (HIV does not cause AIDS). Saying only that the body's terrain also matters, or naming terrain theory as an approach, is not this narrative.
labels.name: Germ theory is false / terrain theory

concepts: most people don't know they have parasites
do a parasite cleanse once a year
labels.definition: **Hidden parasites cause chronic disease in most people,** including cancer, so routine cleansing or deworming is needed. Advice that everyone should cleanse regularly, even without symptoms, counts.
labels.name: Hidden parasites cause chronic disease

labels.definition: **Undiagnosed heavy-metal burden causes widespread chronic illness,** autism or fatigue, and needs chelation.
labels.name: Hidden heavy-metal toxicity is widespread

labels.definition: **Hidden household mold is widespread and drives chronic illness,** including bowel disease.
labels.name: Hidden mold toxicity is widespread

concepts: it's all about the Epstein-Barr virus
undiagnosed infections silently causing chronic disease
labels.definition: **Hidden chronic infections underlie most chronic disease.** EBV, mycoplasma, Lyme co-infections or other "stealth" pathogens are blamed; Lyme alone is `narrative:chronic_lyme_widespread`. A hidden infection as the cause of one named disease (EBV in Hashimoto's or MS) is not this narrative.

labels.definition: **Mitochondrial or metabolic dysfunction is the root cause of nearly all chronic disease.**
labels.name: Metabolic dysfunction is the root of all disease

concepts: inflammation is the root of all disease
labels.definition: **Chronic inflammation is the root cause of all or most disease.** Inflammation as the cause of one specific disease is not this narrative.
labels.name: Inflammation is the root of all disease

concepts: your body can't keep up with the toxins
labels.definition: **The body accumulates toxins it cannot clear on its own.** "Toxic load", "toxic burden" or an overflowing toxic bucket that must be cleared invokes it; cleanses, detox products or protocols are the usual remedy, but none needs to be named.
labels.name: The body needs help to detox

concepts: all disease begins in the gut
labels.definition: **Leaky gut is the root of disease,** such as autoimmune disease, mental illness, weak immunity or most chronic disease.
labels.name: Leaky gut is the root of disease

labels.definition: **Hidden candida or yeast overgrowth causes chronic illness in many people,** such as fatigue and brain fog.
labels.name: Systemic candida is widespread

concepts: they just renamed adrenal fatigue HPA axis dysfunction

labels.name: Adrenal fatigue is a real condition

labels.definition: **Persistent Lyme infection explains much chronic illness** and needs long-term antibiotics or alternative protocols; it is sometimes called a bioweapon.
labels.name: Chronic Lyme is widespread and needs long treatment

labels.definition: **MTHFR variants cause illness or require methylated supplements.**
labels.name: MTHFR explains chronic illness

labels.definition: **High-dose vitamins cure serious disease** such as sepsis, cancer or autoimmunity. Vitamin megadoses for cancer take this narrative only.

labels.definition: **Methylene blue broadly enhances cognition, mitochondria or longevity.**
labels.name: Methylene blue is a wonder drug

labels.definition: **Red light therapy heals or prevents a wide range of conditions.**
labels.name: Red light therapy heals broadly

labels.definition: **Contact with the earth heals,** transferring electrons that reduce inflammation.
labels.name: Grounding heals

concepts: the most profound healing peptides on the planet
labels.definition: **Research peptides are safe and broadly healing** despite little human evidence. Either half invokes it, including the claim that they are safe to take indefinitely or natural because the body makes them. One specific use claim (BPC-157 for a tendon) is a claim, not this narrative.
labels.name: Peptides are safe miracle healers

labels.definition: **NAD+ boosters or sirtuin activators reverse ageing or broadly restore health.**
labels.name: NAD+ boosters reverse ageing

labels.definition: **Ingested industrial or household chemicals cure disease.** MMS/chlorine dioxide, borax, turpentine, DMSO or colloidal silver are said to cure infections, cancer or autism.
labels.name: Ingested chemicals cure disease

labels.definition: **Frequency, energy, quantum or scalar devices and modalities cure disease.** A device said to heal through combined "frequencies" takes this; add `narrative:grounding_heals` or `narrative:red_light_cure_all` only if their own healing claim is made. PEMF for its cleared uses (bone healing) is a topic.

labels.definition: **Alzheimer's disease can be reversed with lifestyle, dietary or metabolic protocols.** Bredesen's protocol and "type 3 diabetes" are the usual elaborations; calling Alzheimer's "type 3 diabetes" without a reversal or cure claim is not this narrative.

labels.definition: **Autism can be reversed or "recovered" through diet, detox or biomedical protocols.** Leucovorin alone is `narrative:leucovorin_autism_treatment`.
